newsitem.title: USA: CME traders say USDA Cattle-on-Feed data bearish.
newsitem.headline: CME traders say USDA Cattle-on-Feed data bearish.

text.p: CME traders said the U.S. Department of Agriculture's monthly Cattle-on-Feed Report was bearish for live cattle futures.
February was seen opening around 0.40 to 0.50 cent a lb lower Monday based on the data with the back months about 0.50 to 0.75 cent a lb down.
The report was also seen weighing on the nearby December contract although Monday's cash trend was expected to be the dominant market factor for the first position.

USDA put the number of cattle on feed in the leading seven states, as of November 1, at 101 percent of a year ago, above all estimates in a Reuter survey of analysts which ranged from 97.6 to 100.5 percent and averaged 99.5 percent.
October placements at 111 percent of a year ago also were above all estimates. Survey estimates ranged form 101.2 to 110.0 percent and averaged 105.7 percent.
October marketings at 93 percent were below all estimates which ranged from 95.5 to 100.0 percent and averaged 97.3.
"We didn't market enough and we placed more cattle," said independent analyst Phil Stanley.
Traders said the placement figure was particularly bearish and so deferred contracts would probably show the largest losses when the futures market reopens on Monday.
